title: Indoor coverage creates a privacy-versus-context tension
content: Richer indoor context usually requires cameras or microphones, while privacy-sensitive households may reject those sensors in bedrooms and other intimate spaces.

title: Fragmented alerts increase interpretation burden
content: Separate motion, door, lock and camera notifications require users to reconstruct whether several signals belong to one incident.

title: False alarms erode trust in home security
content: Pet motion, weather, shadows and routine household activity can create alerts that teach users to ignore future notifications.

title: Detached homes create perimeter and multi-entry needs
content: Suburban detached-home layouts commonly create front-door, side-yard, garage and backyard security zones that benefit from cross-device context.

title: Dense apartments shift value toward entry and shared-space security
content: Urban apartment households place relatively more emphasis on the entry door, packages, shared corridors, compact installation and neighbor privacy than on large outdoor perimeters.

title: Subscription acceptance varies by value clarity
content: A recurring security service must provide continuous and legible value; local-first hardware can differentiate where households resist mandatory cloud subscriptions.

title: AI actions require explicit safety boundaries
content: Device-affecting AI decisions should distinguish recommendations, reversible automations and high-impact actions requiring human confirmation and audit records.

title: Regional privacy requirements affect product architecture
content: Products handling household identity, audio, video or behavioral data need data minimization, explicit purpose and region-aware retention and consent controls.
